Rarity.maps_to: Potion.rarity = 'common' (potions.py:471), read by shop.MerchantPotionEntry pricing and by potion_pools.POTION_POOL's rarity bucket (potion_pools.py:38-65)
Rarity.rationale: EXECUTED, not asserted: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-attrs` extracts PotionRarity from every C# model and diffs it against the sim class attribute over all 51 units and reports 0 mismatches. Rarity is observable in the sim (it sets the shop price and the reward-roll bucket), so this is a behavioural verdict rather than a field copy.

Usage.maps_to: no explicit attribute; the sim's only potion-use entry point is CombatState.use_potion (combat.py:583-616), which cannot be reached outside a combat
Usage.rationale: PotionUsage.CombatOnly means the game's Use button is live only during a fight. The sim reaches that by construction: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-usage` finds exactly one `def use_potion` in sts2_rl/, on CombatState, and the conformance driver only dispatches the recording's UsePotion command inside a live fight (conformance/combat_driver.py:16,263-289). The absence of a `usage` attribute is therefore not a dropped guard for this unit -- but it IS a real gap for the four AnyTime potions, which is where the divergence is filed (blood_potion, entropic_brew, foul_potion, fruit_juice).

TargetType.maps_to: no attribute -- `targeted` stays False, so CombatState.use_potion passes target=None (combat.py:608) and the potion applies to ctx.player (potions.py:474-488)
TargetType.rationale: TargetType.Self in a single-player run always resolves to the owner: PotionModel.EnqueueManualUse defaults `target` to `Owner.Creature` when it is a valid target (PotionModel.cs:240-243) and IsValidTarget's Self/AnyPlayer arms accept exactly that creature (PotionModel.cs:280-287). The multiplayer half -- AnyPlayer letting you throw the potion at an ally, and CanThrowAtAlly (PotionModel.cs:381-388) gating it on `RunState.Players.Count > 1` -- is out of scope by the shared contract and noted in maps_to rather than verdicted as a divergence.

OnUse (protected override, AttackPotion..issue: Rollup of guards G1 and N per binding rule 4. The generation half is right -- the Ironclad pool filtered to Type == Attack, three distinct cards off Rng.CombatCardGeneration -- and the parity arm defers the pick to the recording; the legacy arm skips the choose-a-card screen entirely (G1) and the shared FilterForCombat port is missing its Event-rarity clause (N).

guards.what: N1: the generation draw -- `CardFactory.GetDistinctForCombat(Owner, pool, 3, RunState.Rng.CombatCardGeneration)` vs get_distinct_for_combat_parity
guards.rationale: GetDistinctForCombat is `FilterForCombat(cards).TakeRandom(count, rng)` (CardFactory.cs:119-129), and TakeRandom is an UnstableShuffle of the filtered list followed by Take(n). cards/pool.py:182-204's get_distinct_for_combat_parity does exactly that -- `pool_card_ids(...)`, `rng.shuffle(ids)` through the GameRandomAdapter's top-down Fisher-Yates, `ids[:count]` -- so the draw COUNT and the stream match, which is what a grade-A stream desync would break. The rng named in the C# is Rng.CombatCardGeneration and the sim reads combat.combat_rng.card_gen, the same stream (PROMPT.md bug class 16 checks whether the stream is consumed, and here it is, once per generation).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): outside a parity replay the sim never offers the choose-a-card screen -- it silently takes the FIRST generated card and cannot skip
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the C# hands the three generated cards to `CardSelectCmd.FromChooseACardScreen(choiceContext, cards, Owner, canSkip: true)` and adds the RESULT, which may be null (the player skipped) -- CardSelectCmd.cs:216-261, and the caller's `if (cardModel != null)` guard. The sim forks on `combat.combat_rng.is_parity`: the parity arm defers correctly to CombatState.offer_screen_selection (combat.py:618-637), which the recording's `SelectCardFromScreen` resolves and whose non-numeric 'skip' arg is honoured (conformance/combat_driver.py:290-295); the LEGACY arm takes `cards[0]` unconditionally. Both the RL env and every non-parity test take the legacy arm (full_env.py:788 constructs the env without an rng_set), so in training the potion is deterministic in the generated order and the other two candidates and the skip option do not exist. LIVE: all five card-generating potions are ported and in the reward pool, and the divergence is a different CARD entering the hand, which the observation encoder sees. Shared mechanism across attack_potion, skill_potion, power_potion and colorless_potion (orobic_acid has no screen and is not a site).

guards.what: N: CardFactory.FilterForCombat drops three rarities and the sim's pool_card_ids drops only two
guards.issue: CardFactory.FilterForCombat is `c.CanBeGeneratedInCombat && c.Rarity != Basic && c.Rarity != Ancient && c.Rarity != Event` then `.Distinct()` (CardFactory.cs:159-162). cards/pool.py:108-117's pool_card_ids checks BASIC and ANCIENT and `can_be_generated_in_combat`, and has no EVENT clause. DORMANT, executed: over both pools the sim reaches through this potion family, no card carries a non-Common/Uncommon/Rare rarity at all -- IRONCLAD_POOL 85 ids -> 78 after the filter, COLORLESS_POOL 53 -> 50, and the EVENT bucket is empty in each. What would make it live: porting any Event-rarity card into IRONCLAD_POOL or COLORLESS_POOL, at which point it becomes an offerable candidate in the sim and is not one in the game, changing both the offer AND the UnstableShuffle draw the parity path takes over the filtered list. CROSS-STREAM: pool.py is shared with the card tier; reported rather than fixed.

guards.rationale: Both arms of the sim do the same two things in the same order -- card.set_free_this_turn() (cards/base.py:260-263, the SetToFreeThisTurn counterpart) then CardPileCmd.add_to_hand (cmds.py:500) -- the parity arm inside CombatState.resolve_screen_selection (combat.py:635-637) and the legacy arm inline. The free cost expires at the player's next turn start (player.py:154-155 reset_turn_cost_modifiers), matching 'free this turn'.

guards.what: N3: the potion has no CanonicalVars and no numeric constant; the `3` is a literal argument
guards.rationale: `py audit/tools/potion_probes.py sweep-vars` reports no DynamicVar for this unit. The count 3 appears as a literal in both the C# call and the sim call, and there is no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension anywhere in the file, so there is no non-ascension branch to prefer.

guards.what: W: the shared PotionModel.OnUseWrapper pipeline every potion resolves through (audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md)
guards.issue: MECHANISM, shared by all 51 units and recorded once per record because PotionModel is one of harness.py's MODEL_ROOT_CLASSES, so no unit record enumerates it -- and unlike CardModel/PowerModel/RelicModel it is NOT covered by any seam record either, which is the coverage hole audit/content/potion/shared-mechanisms.md exists to name. src/Core/Models/PotionModel.cs:291-342 in order: :293 RemoveBeforeUse (sim combat.py:603-606 nulls the slot and detaches the listener before the effect -- faithful); :297 Hook.BeforePotionUsed; :327 OnUse (this record's own hooks); :336 CombatManager.History.PotionUsed (no sim entry -- PotionUsedEntry.cs:9-38 adds only a Description string and an executed grep of src/ finds no game reader, so presentation only); :338 Hook.AfterPotionUsed (sim hooks.py:566-571 on_potion_used, dispatched at combat.py:610 -- faithful); :340 CheckForEmptyHand. TWO of those are LIVE gaps, and both are already owned by another record, so this entry MATCHES their verdicts per binding rule 3 rather than re-deriving them. (1) BeforePotionUsed has no sim dispatcher at all -- hooks.py declares only on_potion_used, whose own docstring says it mirrors AfterPotionUsed -- and its single C# implementer SurroundedPower.cs:82 is ported at powers.py:2523, so throwing a potion at the far Kaiser Crab arm does not turn the player to face it: audit/records/power/surrounded.json, gap, live. (2) CombatManager.cs:887-893 CheckForEmptyHand has exactly two callers, CardModel.cs:1992 and PotionModel.cs:340, and the sim's only on_hand_emptied call site is player.py:197 -- the end-of-turn flush CombatManager.cs:880-883 explicitly excludes: audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G1, gap, LIVE, executed with a potion witness. Reachable from EVERY potion, not only the hand-emptying ones, because C# tests the hand AFTER the use. Rollup `gap` per binding rule 4.

guards.what: W4: PotionModel.cs:324-331 brackets OnUse in BeginCardOrPotionEffect/EndCardOrPotionEffect and the sim has no re-entrancy depth counter
guards.issue: CombatManager.cs:889's `!IsExecutingCardOrPotionEffect(player)` is what stops a nested effect from triggering the empty-hand check early, and PotionModel.cs:324-331 is what puts a potion inside that bracket. The sim has no counterpart anywhere. DORMANT for the same reason audit/records/relic/unceasing_top.json G2 is dormant -- the ported cards that auto-play another card mid-resolution (cards/cascade.py:58, cards/colorless_skills.py:117) do not touch the draw pile between the inner and outer ends -- but recorded separately because the OUTER frame here is a potion, so a fix that brackets only card plays would leave this half open. What would make it live: any ported potion or card that empties the hand and then moves the draw pile from inside a nested auto-play.
